6661.title: Palm Pilot
6661.heading: Palm Pilot
6661.content:
The Palm Pilot was a handheld organizer introduced in 1996 with a deliberately simple interface. It replaced paper address books, calendars, task lists, and notebooks with synchronized digital records.

Careful attention to a limited set of common activities made the device approachable. Its success established personal digital assistants as a path toward smartphones.

6664.title: Pair Programming
6664.heading: Pair Programming
6664.content:
Pair programming has two developers work together at one workstation on the same change. One concentrates on the immediate implementation while the other reviews, anticipates consequences, and keeps the wider design in view; the roles rotate frequently.

The practice provides continuous review, spreads knowledge, and supports test-driven work. Its output includes shared understanding as well as code.

6667.title: Pairing Method for Arithmetic Sums
6667.heading: Pairing Method for Arithmetic Sums
6667.content:
The pairing method for arithmetic sums combines terms equally far from opposite ends of an [[Arithmetic Progression]]. Each pair has the same total.

For (1+2+\cdots+100), pairing (1) with (100), (2) with (99), and so on gives fifty pairs of (101), so the sum is (50\cdot101=5050). Equivalently, write the sum forward and backward, add the two rows to obtain one hundred copies of (101), and divide by two. The method exposes structure that direct accumulation hides.

6673.title: PageRank
6673.heading: PageRank
6673.content:
PageRank is an algorithm that ranks web pages by interpreting hyperlinks as weighted endorsements. A page receives importance from its [[Backlink|backlinks]], and each source page divides its own importance evenly among its outgoing links.

The method represents the web as a [[Web Graph]], forms a [[Google Matrix]], and applies the [[Power Method]] until the [[PageRank Vector]] converges. The final values are relative and sum to one, allowing pages to be ordered by structural importance.

In a distributed dataflow implementation, each iteration emits outgoing links and partial rank contributions, groups contributions by destination, and stores or exchanges the revised ranks. Caching the graph and communicating updates collectively avoids rereading the unchanged network during every round.

6675.sourceSearchName: page rank vector page rank vector
6675.title: PageRank Vector
6675.heading: Document

6676.sourceSearchName: page rank vector page rank vector
6676.title: PageRank Vector
6676.heading: PageRank Vector
6676.content:
A PageRank vector contains one relative-importance value for every page in a [[Web Graph]]. Its values sum to one, so each entry expresses a page's share of the graph's total rank.

The vector begins with an initial distribution and is repeatedly multiplied by the [[Google Matrix]]. When further multiplication no longer changes it, the vector has converged to an [[Eigenvector]] whose values supply the final [[PageRank]] ordering.

6679.sourceSearchName: page rank teleportation page rank teleportation
6679.title: PageRank Teleportation
6679.heading: PageRank Teleportation
6679.content:
PageRank teleportation gives the [[Random Surfer Model|random surfer]] a nonzero probability of jumping to any page instead of following an outgoing link. The remaining probability is assigned to normal movement through the web's link structure.

This adjustment prevents rank from becoming trapped in a [[Link Sink]] and makes every destination reachable in the transition model. Combining link-following and teleportation probabilities produces the [[Google Matrix]].

6682.title: Packet Switching
6682.heading: Packet Switching
6682.content:
Packet switching divides a message into smaller addressed units that may travel independently through a network and be reassembled at the destination. Links can be shared among many conversations instead of reserved for one circuit.

The method uses network capacity flexibly and can route around unavailable paths. It differed sharply from the dedicated circuits developed for traditional telephone service.

6685.heading: Packet Inspection
6685.content:
Packet inspection examines captured network frames and decodes their link, network, transport, and application protocol fields. It can reveal addresses, ports, flags, sequence information, payload sizes, and timing that application logs omit.

Inspection is diagnostic evidence rather than an explanation by itself. Captures should be filtered to the relevant conversation and handled carefully because payloads can contain credentials or sensitive application data.

6688.title: Package Dependency
6688.heading: Package Dependency
6688.content:
A package dependency exists when one software package requires functions or data supplied by another. Installing an R package may therefore install or require several supporting packages before the requested functionality can run.

Dependencies make modular software reuse possible, but they also expand the version combinations that must be managed. A reproducible analysis should record the packages and versions it relies on, especially when moving from an exploratory workstation to a production environment.

6691.title: P-Value
6691.heading: P-Value
6691.content:
A p-value is the probability, under a specified [[Null Hypothesis]], of obtaining a test statistic at least as extreme as the observed one. It measures incompatibility with the null model rather than the probability that the null hypothesis is true.

The value is itself a [[Random Variable]] across repeated studies. It should be reported with an [[Effect Size]] and uncertainty because statistical significance alone does not establish scientific importance.

6694.heading: P-Type Semiconductor
6694.content: A p-type semiconductor has acceptor impurity levels near the valence band. Electrons can move into those levels, leaving mobile electron vacancies called holes that behave as positive charge carriers. It is one side of a photovoltaic [[P-N Junction]]. P-type behavior depends on the type and concentration of impurities introduced through [[Semiconductor Doping]].

6697.title: P-Value Histogram
6697.heading: P-Value Histogram
6697.content:
A p-value histogram summarizes the distribution of p-values across many hypothesis tests. When all null hypotheses are true and tests are calibrated, the values should be approximately uniform; a concentration near zero can indicate a subset of real effects.

Other shapes can reveal model failure, dependence, confounding, or overcorrection. The plot is therefore a diagnostic of the entire analysis rather than a substitute for a multiple-testing procedure.

6700.heading: P-N Junction
6700.content: A p-n junction brings [[P-Type Semiconductor]] and [[N-Type Semiconductor]] regions into contact. The resulting electric field separates electrons and positive holes created when suitable photons are absorbed. With a load connected, their separation gives a usable current. In the source's silicon-cell example, an individual cell supplies roughly half a volt while current depends on receiving area and illumination.

6703.title: P-Hacking
6703.heading: P-Hacking
6703.content:
P-hacking is the use of flexible analytic choices to obtain or emphasize statistically significant results. It can include trying many variables, exclusions, transformations, interaction terms, or model specifications without accounting for the search.

The problem is not exploration itself but presenting searched-for evidence as a single prespecified test. Defenses include an [[A Priori Hypothesis]], a documented analytic plan, honest labeling of exploratory findings, and validation in independent data.

6705.heading: Document

6706.sourceSearchName: p adic valuation p adic valuation
6706.title: p-Adic Valuation
6706.heading: p-Adic Valuation
6706.content:
For a chosen prime p, the p-adic valuation of a nonzero integer is the exponent of the highest power of p dividing it. For a rational numerator divided by denominator, the valuation is the numerator's exponent minus the denominator's. The associated p-adic norm is p raised to the negative valuation.

This reverses ordinary magnitude intuitions: a number divisible by a very high power of p is small in the p-adic norm. The resulting non-Archimedean distance expresses closeness through shared divisibility or prefix structure and supports a hierarchical topology.

6712.heading: p-Adic Dendrogram Encoding
6712.content:
The book encodes a leaf's root-to-terminal route by placing signed branch labels at powers of a chosen base. Coefficients are -1, 0, or +1, with nonzero terms recording the nodes along that route. The resulting code is a compact numeric representation of a ranked binary dendrogram.

Using a base of at least 3 avoids ambiguous ordinary-integer equivalents for these signed coefficients, and the tree can be reconstructed from the unique codes. Exchanging left and right branch labels changes individual codes while preserving the underlying cluster nesting.

Overlapping community detection allows one vertex to participate in several network groups. The model fits systems in which a person, protein, document, or resource serves multiple roles.

Membership can be represented through shared cliques, link communities, latent factors, or fractional weights. Evaluation is harder than for a partition because both the group boundaries and the degree of overlap must be assessed.

6718.title: Overlapping Clusters
6718.heading: Overlapping Clusters
6718.content:
Overlapping clusters permit an observation to participate in more than one group. They are useful when categories have gradual boundaries or when the same case legitimately exhibits characteristics of several clusters.

A fuzzy method represents overlap through membership values rather than forcing a single label. The interpretation must distinguish partial membership from probability: a point can belong to several fuzzy clusters at the same time.

6721.title: Overfitting
6721.heading: Overfitting
6721.content:
Overfitting occurs when a model conforms so closely to its [[Training Dataset]] that it performs poorly on unfamiliar examples. It resembles learning a fixed set of answers by rote without learning the reusable relationship needed to solve new problems.

Additional [[Training Epoch|training epochs]] can continue reducing training error while making generalization worse. Comparing performance against a withheld [[Test Dataset]] reveals this gap and helps determine when more fitting has stopped being useful.

The source illustrates the problem with k-nearest neighbors: using one neighbor classifies every training observation perfectly because each point is its own nearest neighbor, yet it performs poorly on new data. Training fit alone therefore rewards excessive flexibility.

6724.sourceSearchName: overdetermined linear system overdetermined linear system
6724.title: Overdetermined Linear System
6724.heading: Overdetermined Linear System
6724.content:
An overdetermined linear system has more equations than unknowns. Measurement data commonly produce such systems, and an exact solution may not exist.

A [[Least Squares Approximation]] chooses the vector whose predicted right-hand side is closest to the observed one, using a [[Normal Equation]], [[QR Decomposition]], or [[Singular Value Decomposition]].

6727.sourceSearchName: overdetermined least squares overdetermined least squares
6727.title: Overdetermined Least Squares
6727.heading: Overdetermined Least Squares
6727.content:
Overdetermined least squares addresses $Ax=b$ when $A$ has more rows than columns and an exact solution may not exist. It chooses $\hat x$ that minimizes $\|b-Ax\|_2$.

Geometrically, $A\hat x$ is the closest point to $b$ in the column space of $A$, making the residual orthogonal to that space. The computation can use a [[Normal Equation]], [[QR Decomposition]], or SVD.

6733.title: Output Device
6733.heading: Output Device
6733.content:
An output device is a physical device that communicates information from a computer to a user. It is also called a display and may stimulate vision, hearing, touch, smell, taste, or the sense of balance rather than only showing images.

The computer generates or models information and the output device converts it into a perceptible form. In a [[3D User Interface]], the choice of output device affects which [[Interaction Technique]]s are practical. Its [[Display Fidelity]], [[Latency]], resolution, ergonomics, and sensory coverage can all change task performance and [[User Experience]].

6736.title: Outlier
6736.heading: Outlier
6736.content:
An outlier is an observation that deviates enough from other observations to suggest it may have arisen from a different mechanism. It can be an error, a rare valid case, or evidence of a distinct process.

Declaring a point anomalous requires an explicit reference context. Global distance, local density, statistical probability, and cluster membership can produce different judgments.

In life-science measurements, an outlier can arise from an undesired technical process such as scanner damage or amplification bias. The source demonstrates that one extreme value can severely distort the sample mean, variance, correlation, and t-test, motivating robust and rank-based alternatives.

6739.title: Outlier Detection
6739.heading: Outlier Detection
6739.content:
Outlier detection identifies observations whose relationship to the rest of a data set is unusually weak or structurally different. Methods can use distributions, pairwise distance, neighborhood density, clustering, or fuzzy membership.

Detection is a screening step rather than automatic deletion. Suspected cases should be investigated because correcting an error and erasing a rare event have very different consequences.

6742.sourceSearchName: outcome based pricing outcome based pricing
6742.title: Outcome-Based Pricing
6742.heading: Outcome-Based Pricing
6742.content:
Outcome-based pricing rewards a provider when an agreed service outcome is achieved. A bonus might be tied to reduced time to market, improved availability, or another result that represents the consumer's reason for using the service.

This differs psychologically from a penalty for missing a service level: it pays for success instead of only punishing failure. It is often combined with a fixed base price so the outcome component supplements a stable service contract.

6757.heading: Orthonormal Basis
6757.content:
An orthonormal basis consists of basis vectors that are mutually orthogonal and each have norm one.

Coordinates in such a basis are obtained directly through inner products. Arranging the basis vectors as matrix columns produces an [[Orthogonal Matrix]], which preserves lengths and simplifies projections, QR factorization, and diagonalization.

6760.heading: Otto Cycle Engine Efficiency
6760.content: The ideal Otto cycle models a spark-ignition piston engine with compression, heat addition through combustion, expansion, and exhaust-related heat rejection. Compression and expansion are treated as reversible adiabatic processes, and the enclosed pressure-volume area represents net work. Its ideal efficiency increases with compression ratio and depends on the ratio of specific heats, although real engines also incur friction, heat loss, and incomplete combustion.

6763.title: OSI Model
6763.heading: OSI Model
6763.content:
The Open Systems Interconnection model divides network communication into seven conceptual layers: application, presentation, session, transport, network, data link, and physical. Each layer offers a defined service to the layer above and delegates lower-level work to the layer below.

The model separates responsibilities even when a practical protocol does not mirror every boundary exactly. It provides a vocabulary for locating where formatting, session control, delivery, routing, framing, or signal transmission belongs.

6766.heading: Orthographic and Perspective Views in Blender
6766.content:
Perspective projection resembles ordinary vision: equal-sized objects appear smaller with distance. Orthographic projection removes that size change, so equal dimensions remain visually equal regardless of depth.

Perspective is helpful for judging the final spatial impression, while orthographic views are useful for matching blueprints and controlling proportions. Blender can toggle between them and can jump directly to front, side, top, bottom, or camera views.

6769.title: Orthogonal Vectors
6769.heading: Orthogonal Vectors
6769.content:
Two vectors are orthogonal when their [[Inner Product]] is zero. In Euclidean space this means they meet at a right angle.

A set of nonzero mutually orthogonal vectors is automatically linearly independent. Normalizing their lengths produces an [[Orthonormal Basis]].

6772.title: Orthogonal Projection
6772.heading: Orthogonal Projection
6772.content:
An orthogonal projection maps a point to the closest point in a specified linear subspace. The difference between the original and projected point is perpendicular to that subspace, which minimizes squared reconstruction distance.

Projecting samples onto selected basis directions produces lower-dimensional coordinates. In principal-component analysis, the chosen subspace maximizes retained variation and minimizes squared reconstruction error among linear subspaces of the same dimension.

6775.title: Orthogonal Matrix
6775.heading: Orthogonal Matrix
6775.content:
A real square matrix $Q$ is orthogonal when $Q^TQ=QQ^T=I$, so $Q^{-1}=Q^T$. Its columns and rows form orthonormal sets.

Orthogonal transformations preserve vector lengths and angles. This makes them numerically valuable in [[QR Decomposition]], [[Orthogonal Diagonalization]], [[Givens Rotation]], and [[Householder Transformation]].

6778.title: Orthogonal Diagonalization
6778.heading: Orthogonal Diagonalization
6778.content:
Orthogonal diagonalization represents a real symmetric matrix as $A=QDQ^T$, where $Q$ is orthogonal and $D$ is diagonal.

The columns of $Q$ are orthonormal eigenvectors, so changing coordinates preserves lengths and angles. This is stronger than ordinary [[Matrix Diagonalization]] and is available for real [[Symmetric Matrix|symmetric matrices]].

6781.title: Orthogonal Clustering View
6781.heading: Orthogonal Clustering View
6781.content:
An orthogonal clustering view seeks a projection whose directions carry little or no overlap with those supporting a prior clustering. Clusters found in that projection emphasize variance hidden from the original view.

Geometric orthogonality provides a clear diversity criterion for numeric data, but it is stronger than semantic difference and may discard useful shared information. The new projection still requires an independent cohesion and stability assessment.

6784.title: Orphaned Verb
6784.heading: Orphaned Verb
6784.content:
An orphaned verb is a [[Game Verb]] with little or no relationship to the rest of a game's interactive vocabulary. It may be used for one isolated action and then forgotten because other rules do not reinforce or develop it.

Orphaned verbs increase [[Cognitive Load]] without creating much depth. A design can avoid them by making its important verbs serve multiple purposes and interact with multiple objects, rather than adding a new control for every special case.

6787.title: Organoid
6787.heading: Organoid
6787.content:
An organoid is a three-dimensional tissue model produced when stem cells differentiate and self-organize into structures that reproduce selected features of an organ. Developmental programs create architecture rather than a printer placing every cell directly.

Organoids capture useful multicellular behavior but vary between samples and remain incomplete representations of mature whole organs.

6790.heading: Oriented Bounding Box
6790.content:
An oriented bounding box is a rectangular collision volume whose axes can rotate with the enclosed object. It usually fits a rotated model more closely than an [[Axis-Aligned Bounding Box]].

The improved fit makes intersection tests more expensive because overlap must be evaluated along candidate separating axes rather than by comparing world-axis intervals alone.

6793.heading: Organ-on-a-Chip
6793.content:
An organ-on-a-chip is a small engineered tissue model designed to reproduce selected structures and functions of an organ within a controlled device. Microfluidic flow and mechanical or biochemical inputs create conditions difficult to maintain in an ordinary culture dish.

The model is intentionally partial: it is useful when the reproduced function matches the biological question or therapy being tested.

6796.content:
An organoid-on-a-chip combines stem-cell self-organization with the controlled flow and stimulation of a microfluidic device. The organoid supplies complex tissue development, while the chip regulates transport and exposes measurable environmental conditions.

The integration can improve maturation and experimental control but inherits variability from organoids and interface complexity from microfluidics.

6799.title: Ordinal Feature
6799.heading: Ordinal Feature
6799.content:
An ordinal feature takes values from a set with a meaningful order but without guaranteed numerical spacing. Educational degrees can be ordered from bachelor to master to doctorate, yet the gaps between those levels are not measurable as equal quantities.

Algorithms may exploit the ranking while avoiding arithmetic interpretations that the scale does not support. Treating an ordinal variable as either unordered categories or fully quantitative values discards or invents structure.

6808.content:
An ordered classification rule belongs to a priority list of if-then conditions. Prediction tests rules in sequence and uses the consequent of the first antecedent satisfied by the observation.

Ordering resolves conflicts without combining every matching rule, but it makes a rule's meaning depend on all earlier entries. A default rule at the end supplies a class for cases that satisfy no learned condition.

6811.title: ORCLUS Clustering
6811.heading: ORCLUS Clustering
6811.content:
ORCLUS finds projected clusters in arbitrarily oriented subspaces. It begins with many seed clusters in the full space, estimates low-variance directions, and repeatedly merges clusters while reducing both the cluster count and subspace dimensionality.

Local covariance eigenvectors define each cluster's preferred orientation. This captures correlated structures beyond axis-parallel methods, but covariance estimation can be unstable for small or noisy intermediate groups.

6814.title: Orbiting Panning and Zooming in Blender
6814.heading: Orbiting Panning and Zooming in Blender
6814.content:
The 3D Viewport is a two-dimensional window onto a three-dimensional scene. Orbiting rotates the apparent world around a fixed point, panning shifts the view laterally, and zooming changes how much of the scene is visible.

Thinking of the scene as moving in front of the viewer clarifies these controls. Navigation changes the point of view, not the scene objects themselves, so it can be used freely while modeling or inspecting spatial relationships.

6820.sourceSearchName: orbital velocity and period orbital velocity and period
6820.title: Orbital Velocity and Period
6820.heading: Orbital Velocity and Period
6820.content: In a circular orbit, gravitational attraction supplies the required centripetal force. The orbital speed depends on the parent body's gravitational parameter and the orbital radius, while the period grows with the three-halves power of that radius. These relations assume negligible atmospheric drag and are special cases of the energy relation in [[Vis-Viva Orbital Energy Relation]].

6821.sourceSearchName: orbital velocity and period orbital velocity and period
6821.title: Orbital Velocity and Period
6821.heading: References

6823.title: Orbital Motion
6823.heading: Orbital Motion
6823.content: An orbit is continuous [[Free Fall]] in which gravity bends motion around a central body. For a circular orbit, setting gravitational force equal to the required centripetal force gives $v=\sqrt{GM/r}$ and $T^2=4\pi^2r^3/(GM)$. Higher circular orbits have lower speed but longer period.

6826.title: Orbit Camera
6826.heading: Orbit Camera
6826.content:
An orbit camera revolves around a target while maintaining a radial distance. Its state is naturally stored with horizontal and vertical angles plus distance rather than as an unconstrained world position.

Those spherical parameters are converted into a camera position each update, and the camera looks back toward the target. Angle and distance limits prevent unwanted flips, clipping, or movement through the target.

6829.title: Optional Prop
6829.heading: Optional Prop
6829.content:
An optional prop is a component input that the consumer may omit. In a TypeScript props interface, the optional marker distinguishes it from inputs every use of the component must supply.

The component must define behavior for the missing value. It may render nothing for that feature, select a [[Default Prop|default value]], or derive the behavior from other inputs.

6832.title: Optogenetic Muscle Control
6832.heading: Optogenetic Muscle Control
6832.content:
Optogenetic muscle control activates genetically modified muscle with patterned light. Illuminating one side of a symmetric robot creates an asymmetric contraction and directional movement, while a moving light pattern can generate a coordinated wave.

The method enables remote spatial control but requires genetic modification, optical access, compatible wavelengths, and careful exposure levels.

6835.title: Optogenetics
6835.heading: Optogenetics
6835.content:
Optogenetics genetically equips cells with light-sensitive proteins so illumination changes their electrical or biochemical activity. Light can be directed in space and time more precisely than an electric field spread through culture medium.

In biohybrid robotics, optogenetic muscle turns a focused pulse into a localized contraction used for steering or selective actuation.

6838.title: Optimal Solution
6838.heading: Optimal Solution
6838.content:
An optimal solution is a [[Feasible Solution]] whose objective value is no worse than that of every other feasible point.

A linear program may have one optimum, several tied optima, no feasible solution, or an unbounded objective. For a solvable linear program, at least one optimum occurs at a basic feasible extreme point.

6841.title: Optimistic Concurrency
6841.heading: Optimistic Concurrency
6841.content: Optimistic concurrency allows work to proceed without holding a lock, then verifies at commit time that the persisted [[Aggregate]] has not changed since it was read. A version value is loaded with the aggregate and supplied as the expected version when saving. If another command committed first, the mismatch rejects the stale write instead of overwriting it. In [[Event Sourcing]], the number or revision of events in an [[Event Stream]] provides the aggregate version naturally.

6844.sourceSearchName: optimal stopping problem optimal stopping problem
6844.title: Optimal Stopping Problem
6844.heading: Optimal Stopping Problem
6844.content:
An optimal stopping problem asks when to stop examining sequentially arriving options in order to maximize a reward or minimize a cost. Each decision must account for the danger of accepting too early and the danger of passing the best option.

The defining constraint is that rejected choices cannot later be recovered. The [[Secretary Problem]] gives a concrete strategy: reserve an initial sample for comparison, then accept the first later candidate that exceeds that benchmark.

6847.title: Optical See-Through Display
6847.heading: Optical See-Through Display
6847.content:
An optical see-through display combines a direct view of the physical world with generated light by means of an optical combiner. The user sees real objects through the display while virtual imagery is reflected or projected into the same line of sight.

Because the real view does not pass through a camera, it retains natural resolution and low visual delay. The virtual camera must be calibrated to the user's eye, and the system has limited control over real-world brightness, focus, and occlusion.

6850.title: Optical Tracking
6850.heading: Optical Tracking
6850.content:
Optical tracking estimates the position or orientation of cameras, objects, or users from captured light. A system may observe prepared markers, active light sources, reflective targets, or natural image features.

Cameras are readily available on mobile AR devices and can relate measurements directly to visible scene structure. Performance depends on illumination, visibility, feature quality, camera calibration, computation, and the ability to recover after the target leaves view.

A reachability plot exposes valleys corresponding to clusters over a range of density thresholds instead of committing to one global cut. Interpretation or a subsequent extraction rule is still needed to turn the ordering into a final partition.

6859.title: Opposite Number
6859.heading: Opposite Number
6859.content:
The opposite of a number (a) is the number (-a) that combines with it to produce the additive identity:

$$a+(-a)=0.$$

Opposites lie the same distance from zero on opposite sides of the [[Number Line]]. Taking the opposite twice returns the original value, so (-(-a)=a). The notation does not say a number is negative by itself: if (a<0), then (-a>0). Subtraction can be defined as addition of an opposite, (a-b=a+(-b)).

6862.title: Opportunity Cost
6862.heading: Opportunity Cost
6862.content:
Opportunity cost is the value forgone when resources are committed to one choice instead of the best available alternative. Capital tied up in computing capacity cannot be used for another investment, even if the purchased capacity remains idle.

Cloud services can reduce this cost by converting some up-front acquisition into flexible operating expense. The comparison must also include the opportunity loss caused when insufficient capacity prevents the organization from meeting demand.

6886.heading: OpenGL Drawing in Blender
6886.content:
OpenGL-style drawing in Blender can place transient lines and shapes over a 3D Viewport without adding mesh objects to the scene. A draw callback enables the required graphics state, issues line or vertex commands in canvas coordinates, and then disables or resets that state.

Restoring defaults after every draw helps the overlay cooperate with Blender and other add-ons that share the graphics context. Because the source targets Blender 2.78c and OpenGL 2.1-style `bgl`, exact functions are version-specific, but disciplined state management remains a general requirement for shared viewport drawing.

Core editor code can avoid direct OpenGL calls by using Blender's GPU abstraction. The tutorial editor clears a region and emits colored rectangles through [[Blender Immediate-Mode GPU Drawing]], allowing the [[Blender Region Draw Dispatch]] path to render through application-owned shaders, buffers, and state.

6895.content:
An open-source game engine exposes its source and grants reuse under its license, but engines still differ in editor workflow, scripting language, renderer, platform support, asset formats, and integration with Blender.

Selection should follow project needs and the team's ability to validate the complete asset path. Godot emphasizes a standalone node-based editor, Stride offers a modular C# toolchain, and Armory3D integrates game production more directly into Blender.

6901.title: Open-Closed Principle
6901.heading: Open-Closed Principle
6901.content: The open-closed principle favors extending behavior through a defined contract while keeping established client-facing behavior stable. A caller that depends on an interface can accept a new implementation without rewriting the caller for each variant. The useful boundary is the one likely to vary; adding an interface for every class before variation appears can make the design more complex without improving extensibility.

6904.title: Open-Cycle MHD System
6904.heading: Open-Cycle MHD System
6904.content: An open-cycle MHD system burns fuel to make a hot gas stream, adds an ionizing seed, accelerates the gas through a nozzle, and extracts direct current in an [[MHD Generator Duct]]. Exhaust heat preheats incoming oxidant; seed recovery and pollution control precede discharge. Unlike a [[Closed-Cycle MHD System]], the working gas is not continuously recirculated through the same loop.

6907.title: Open Story
6907.heading: Open Story
6907.content:
An open story is an emergent narrative with relatively few controlled outcomes and substantial room for players to create their own experiences. The creator facilitates a space in which stories can arise rather than determining which story must be delivered.

Open stories trade authorial control for variety and unpredictability. They may emerge from complex systems, player-created goals, shared authorship, or multiplayer interaction, and they need not resemble a polished traditional plot to be worth retelling.

6910.title: Open Resistance
6910.heading: Open Resistance
6910.content:
Open resistance gives players substantial control over where, when, and why they encounter challenge. Openness may come from several routes through a world, a larger palette of verbs, optional goals, or a system in which players invent goals of their own.

An open game is still shaped by rules rather than being a blank canvas. Its [[Possibility Space]] determines what can be built or pursued, while players decide which possibilities become their particular experience.
